notes: Switching to a slice fixes the reported root-module for_each case. However, it still dedups by ConfigResource across modules instead of by instance at expansion time, so a child-module import of a different instance (or of a different module instance) is still silently dropped whenever the parent imports any instance of that resource, which is likely why 2 of 3 hidden tests fail; the added test covers only the root case.

Fixes the reported root-module for_each case by returning a slice, but it still dedupes parent and child import blocks per ConfigResource instead of per resource instance. A child-module import for a different instance than the parent's is therefore still silently dropped (the same bug class the issue reports), and only 1/3 hidden tests pass. The reference instead moves dedup into expandResourceImports, keyed on the instance.

Fixes the reported case by making quoted braces non-structural in NextArg/NextBlock and in the main parser paths (directives, directive, open/close brace checks, blockTokens), with focused regression tests including the backtick form. It misses the brace handling in doImport's nesting and snippet-detection switch, where a quoted brace in an imported snippet can leave maybeSnippet stuck on, and also misses the anonymous-block check, addresses(), and ArgErr. It also defines duplicate isOpenBrace/isCloseBrace methods on parser, even though parser already embeds *Dispenser.

This fixes the reported case by treating only unquoted braces as delimiters in the dispenser and in the main parser paths (`directive`, `directives`, `blockTokens`, `open`/`closeCurlyBrace`). It misses `doImport`'s nesting switch, the anonymous-block check, `addresses()` and `ArgErr`, and leaves quoted `"{}"` able to skip the newline break. It also duplicates `isOpenBrace`/`isCloseBrace` on `parser`, which already embeds `*Dispenser`. The added parse tests cover unbalanced quoted braces sensibly, including the backtick case.

The patch walks up the section chain and substitutes slugs, which handles the issue's example plus pages and sub-sections under a slugged section, but it has two edge-case bugs. First, using path.Base for each section drops intermediate non-section directories (e.g. /help/a/b when 'a' has no _index) once any ancestor has a slug. Second, it ignores DisablePathToLower by using normalized PathInfo, and the dual Section/SectionBase fallback design is clunkier than a single computed Dir; the tests are solid for sections but don't cover taxonomy or term slugs.

Fixes the issue example correctly and passes the hidden tests, but it bolts a parallel SectionBase field onto the existing Section logic with a cmp.Or fallback and prefix rewriting. Because it rebuilds paths from `path.Base` of each section, intermediate non-section directories are dropped (e.g. /docs/guides/advanced becomes /slug/advanced). It also ignores DisablePathToLower when composing the slugged path.

Adds the flag, rejects conflicting shortcut flags, and rewrites the scenarios after consolidation as the issue asks, but it has gaps: shortcuts in lower layers (env or script, such as K6_ITERATIONS) can wipe the scenarios during the merge so --once silently falls back to the default scenario, the execution-segment flags are not rejected, and exec is always made explicit; unit tests cover the core paths but there are no command-level tests.

Main cases work: default and single-scenario rewrite to 1 VU and 1 iteration, multiple scenarios error, and CLI shortcut conflicts error. However, it only clears shortcuts after the merge, so a higher-layer env/script duration or iterations silently wipes script scenarios and --once then runs default(). It also ignores the execution-segment flags and always sets exec to an explicit "default" instead of preserving the unset value; tests are only small unit tests of the helpers.

The sentinel-error approach works for early returns in partials and for bare returns in templates. However, a return with a value outside a partial is silently accepted instead of erroring, a bare return in a partial yields nil rather than the output so far, and a return inside a `{{ template }}` include exits the whole outer template. Return-argument handling is a narrow IdentifierNode-only rewrite, and the forked exec.go is patched directly without updating the fork script. It also weakens an existing test's assertion to match its own behavior, and the package suite fails.

The core sentinel-error idea works: `return` is a function returning `*ReturnError`, `evalCall` re-panics it and the template store traps it, so early returns work in loops, conditionals and regular templates. Several required edge cases are missing, though. A bare `return` inside a `{{ template }}` call is not trapped at the template boundary, so it ends the whole outer template. `return <value>` outside partials is silently accepted. A non-final `return` in a pipeline silently drops the rest of the pipeline instead of erroring. A bare `return` in a partial now yields nil and discards the output already rendered, which breaks existing partials. The fork-maintenance concerns are not addressed: `errRecover` in the forked `exec.go` is edited directly without updating the fork script, and an AST rewrite (`wrapReturnArgs`) is kept. The candidate changed an existing test's expected error message to fit its own behavior, and the package suite fails.

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference by lifting a parenthesised NumberLiteral into a wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, and it keeps the parse-time positive-duration check for cases like foo[(0)]. However, the wrapping logic is duplicated inline instead of factored into a helper, and DurationExpr.Pretty was not updated, so a unary-plus node would pretty-print with a literal '+'; it adds good round-trip tests and updates the parse_test expectations.

Fixes the round-trip correctly by wrapping a parenthesised NumberLiteral in a unary-plus DurationExpr and keeps the existing parse-time positivity check for `foo[(0)]`; minor gaps are the duplicated wrapping logic instead of a helper, no EndPos, and no Pretty() update to hide the unary plus, but the parse and printer tests are thorough.
